subject: social_science

concepts.title: Dimensions and Social Indicators of Poverty
concepts.section: Poverty as seen by social scientists
concepts.definition: Analyzing deprivation using metrics beyond income, such as literacy levels, healthcare access, sanitation, malnutrition, social exclusion, and vulnerability to economic shocks.
concepts.key_idea: Poverty is multi-dimensional and involves social indicators like exclusion and vulnerability alongside income metrics.
question_patterns: What are the key social indicators used by social scientists to evaluate poverty?
Explain how social exclusion acts as both a cause and a consequence of poverty.
Describe the concept of vulnerability in relation to poverty analysis.
How do non-income factors help in identifying poor households?
Discuss the multi-dimensional aspects of poverty observed in daily life.

solution_steps.explain: Examine illiteracy, lack of healthcare, malnutrition, and absence of clean drinking water.
Assess how poor individuals are excluded from facilities and equal opportunities enjoyed by better-off sections.
Determine the higher risk faced by specific groups during natural disasters or economic downturns.

concepts.title: Poverty Line Determination via Calorie Norms
concepts.definition: A benchmark based on daily minimum nutritional requirements, set at 2400 calories per person daily in rural areas and 2100 calories in urban areas.
concepts.key_idea: Rural calorie norms are higher due to greater physical labor requirements compared to urban regions.
question_patterns: What is the accepted average calorie requirement per person per day in rural India?
Why are daily calorie requirements higher in rural areas than in urban areas?
Explain how minimum food intake is converted into the official poverty line.
How does the National Sample Survey Organisation calculate calorie-based poverty benchmarks?
Calculate or state the difference in calorie intake norms between rural and urban sectors.

solution_steps.explain: Identify rural requirement as 2400 calories per individual daily.
Identify urban requirement as 2100 calories per individual daily.
Rural populations undertake more physical work, demanding higher energy intake.

concepts.title: Monthly Household Poverty Line Threshold
concepts.definition: The minimum monthly family earnings required to stay above the poverty line, calculated by multiplying per capita monthly poverty expenditure by family size.
concepts.key_idea: Total family monetary threshold equals per capita poverty line rate multiplied by family size.
question_patterns: Calculate the monthly poverty threshold for a rural family of given size.
What is the total monthly income needed for an urban family to remain above the poverty line?
Compute the household poverty line requirement for a family with a given per capita expenditure.
Find the minimum monthly earnings needed by a family of several members in rural or urban India.
Determine whether a family falls below the poverty line given their monthly income and family size.

solution_steps.action: multiply per capita rate by family size
solution_steps.explain: The total monthly monetary requirement for the family is per capita monthly rate times number of family members.

concepts.title: MGNREGA Household Wage Earnings Calculation
concepts.definition: The total earnings generated by a rural household under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act based on guaranteed workdays and daily wage rates.
concepts.key_idea: Total wage earned equals daily wage rate multiplied by the number of days employed.
question_patterns: Calculate total earnings of a household working under MGNREGA for a specified number of days.
Find the total wages earned by a worker paid a given daily wage over a set period.
How much money does a household earn if employed for the full 100 days under MGNREGA?
Compute the annual wage payout for a rural worker given daily wage rate and days worked.
Determine the total income generated from MGNREGA employment.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the daily wage rate by the number of days worked.

concepts.title: Poverty Trends and Estimates in India
concepts.definition: The tracking of headcount ratio and total number of impoverished citizens over time using periodic survey data from NSSO.
concepts.key_idea: While the percentage of poor people declined significantly over recent decades, overall population growth kept absolute numbers high for long periods.
question_patterns: Describe the trends in India poverty ratio from 1993-94 to 2011-12.
What was the average annual decline in poverty percentage points between 2004-05 and 2011-12?
Explain why the total number of poor remained high even as poverty percentage dropped.
Analyze table data showing estimates of poverty in India across various survey years.
Discuss how poverty headcount ratios are tracked over time by NSSO.

solution_steps.explain: Observe decline in poverty ratio from 45 percent in 1993-94 to 22 percent in 2011-12.
Note decline from 407 million in 2004-05 to 270 million in 2011-12.
Highlight sustained reduction in both ratio and absolute count in recent years.

concepts.title: Vulnerable Social and Economic Groups
concepts.definition: Social communities like Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, along with economic categories like rural farm laborers and urban casual workers, that suffer disproportionately high poverty rates.
concepts.key_idea: Poverty is unevenly distributed, with socially disadvantaged castes and landless casual laborers facing double jeopardy.
question_patterns: Identify the social groups most vulnerable to poverty in India.
Which economic categories experience the highest poverty levels?
Explain the concept of double disadvantage faced by landless casual workers of backward castes.
Discuss gender and age inequality in resource distribution within poor families.
Who are considered the poorest of the poor within an impoverished household?

solution_steps.explain: Highlight Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe households.
Highlight rural agricultural laborers and urban casual wage workers.
Observe that women, elderly people, and female infants suffer greater deprivation within poor families.

concepts.title: Inter-State Disparities in Poverty
concepts.definition: Uneven poverty distribution across Indian states, where states like Bihar and Odisha report high poverty ratios, while states like Kerala and Punjab show marked reduction.
concepts.key_idea: State-level success in poverty alleviation depends on specific strategies like agricultural growth, human resource focus, land reforms, or public distribution systems.
question_patterns: Describe the inter-state disparities in poverty across India.
Which Indian states continue to report poverty ratios significantly above national average?
How did Punjab and Haryana succeed in reducing poverty?
What strategy enabled Kerala to achieve significant poverty reduction?
Explain the role of land reforms and public distribution systems in state-level poverty reduction.

solution_steps.explain: Bihar and Odisha record the highest headcount ratios above national average.
Punjab relied on agricultural growth, Kerala on human resources, West Bengal on land reforms, and Tamil Nadu on food distribution.

solution_steps.action: compare rural and urban state trends
solution_steps.explain: Observe high urban poverty in states like Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh.

concepts.title: Global Poverty Scenario and Benchmarks
concepts.definition: The assessment of international poverty trends using the World Bank standard of living on less than 1.90 dollars per day per person.
concepts.key_idea: Global poverty has declined overall, led by rapid reductions in China and East Asia, though Sub-Saharan Africa remains heavily impacted.
question_patterns: What benchmark standard does the World Bank use for international poverty comparison?
Describe global trends in poverty reduction since 1990.
How did rapid economic growth affect poverty levels in China and East Asia?
Which global region is projected to hold the largest concentration of extreme poor by 2030?
What is the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal regarding global poverty?

solution_steps.explain: World Bank standard is set at 1.90 US dollars per person per day (2011 PPP).
China and Southeast Asian nations achieved massive reductions through economic expansion.
Sub-Saharan Africa continues to retain high proportions of extreme poverty.

concepts.title: Causes of Poverty in India
concepts.definition: Historical, demographic, structural, and socio-economic factors including colonial ruin of traditional crafts, population pressure, unequal asset distribution, and indebtedness.
concepts.key_idea: Poverty in India stems from a historical legacy of colonial exploitation combined with rapid population growth, inadequate job creation, unequal land ownership, and debt cycles.
question_patterns: What historical factors under British colonial rule contributed to widespread poverty in India?
How do population growth and low economic expansion create a cycle of poverty?
Explain the link between unequal land distribution and rural poverty.
Why does high indebtedness act as both a cause and an effect of poverty?
Discuss socio-cultural factors that force poor families into financial distress.

solution_steps.explain: Colonial policies crippled traditional handicrafts and stifled industrial base.
High population growth paired with limited job growth kept per capita income low.
Unequal land distribution and heavy borrowing for farming inputs and social functions perpetuate debt traps.

concepts.title: Targeted Anti-Poverty Government Programmes
concepts.definition: Specific government initiatives designed to directly reduce poverty through wage employment, credit support, self-employment, and basic infrastructure provisioning.
concepts.key_idea: India anti-poverty strategy balances overall economic growth promotion with direct targeted employment and self-employment schemes like MGNREGA, PMRY, SGSY, and PMGY.
question_patterns: What are the two main planks of the Indian government anti-poverty strategy?
Describe the main features and objectives of MGNREGA 2005.
How do PMRY and REGP promote self-employment in rural areas and small towns?
What is the primary objective of Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)?
Why have anti-poverty programmes yielded mixed results despite good intentions?

solution_steps.explain: Promotion of economic growth and targeted anti-poverty programmes.
MGNREGA for 100-day wage guarantee, PMRY/REGP for youth self-employment, SGSY for self-help groups, PMGY for village services.
Overlapping of schemes and lack of proper targeting reduce overall effectiveness.

concepts.title: Concept of Human Poverty
concepts.definition: Broadening the definition of poverty beyond basic income or food subsistence to include education, healthcare, housing, job security, dignity, and freedom from caste or gender discrimination.
concepts.key_idea: True poverty eradication requires addressing broader human rights, social equality, self-confidence, and dignity beyond mere monetary survival.
question_patterns: What do you understand by the broader concept of human poverty?
How does human poverty differ from minimum subsistence poverty?
Why is poverty eradication considered a moving target as societies develop?
What major socio-economic challenges remain beyond meeting basic income needs?
Explain why providing healthcare and gender equality are essential parts of human poverty eradication.

solution_steps.explain: Subsistence covers minimum food and income, whereas human poverty covers quality of life.
Include literacy, healthcare access, housing security, gender equality, and dignity.
As economic development advances, society baseline expectations for acceptable living expand.
